title: Does iGRPO Need a Good Draft? Best-vs-Worst Self-Conditioning Ablation for RLVR Math

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to isolate whether iGRPO's benefit comes from conditioning on high-quality drafts or from the two-stage structure itself. None of the prior papers explicitly aim to disentangle the source of performance gains in a two-stage reinforcement learning setup by comparing high-quality versus low-quality draft conditioning. While some papers (e.g., [3], [10], [20]) discuss GRPO variants or step-wise policy optimization, they do not explicitly focus on isolating the effects of draft quality versus the two-stage structure. Therefore, no prior paper covers this purpose.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves a controlled ablation comparing three matched-compute conditions: GRPO baseline, iGRPO with best-of-N draft selection, and iGRPO with worst-of-formatted draft selection. Paper [7] conducts an ablation study of deep reinforcement learning in a different domain (congestion control), but the mechanism of matched-compute ablation to isolate the effect of specific components is substantively equivalent. Additionally, [13] performs a matched-compute study to analyze the impact of specific interventions in in-context learning, which is also equivalent in terms of the underlying primitive.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves using identical compute (8 rollouts/prompt, 131 training steps, 2 seeds) across six math benchmarks. Paper [2] evaluates RLVR on six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, which matches the benchmark family and metric semantics. Paper [6] also evaluates a two-stage RL method on a mathematical reasoning benchmark (LexNum). Both papers use similar evaluation designs, so the evaluation facet is covered.

### Domain
The domain is RLVR mathematical reasoning. Papers [1], [2], and [6] all address RLVR in the context of mathematical reasoning, with [6] specifically targeting legal mathematical reasoning. While the specific problem instances and datasets differ, the general application area of RLVR mathematical reasoning is covered.
